title: One-time token can be verified twice concurrently due to missing status predicate in UPDATE query
summary:
## Summary

Logto's one-time token verification contains a TOCTOU race condition. The `verifyOneTimeToken()` function reads a token's status as Active, validates it, then issues an UPDATE query that has no WHERE status = Active predicate. Under PostgreSQL Read Committed isolation, two concurrent transactions can both read Active, both pass validation, and both update the row to Consumed - each returning success to the caller.

## Impact

A one-time password-reset token or magic-link token that should be single-use can be consumed by two concurrent flows:
- Password reset replay: An attacker with the token can race the verification to establish two independent password-reset sessions and call resetPassword() on each to set a password of their choice (account takeover).
- Magic-link dual sign-in: Two tabs loading the same sign-in token URL can both complete sign-in, creating two authenticated sessions from one token.

## Root Cause

packages/core/src/queries/one-time-tokens.ts has an updateOneTimeTokenStatus function that issues:
  UPDATE one_time_tokens SET status = Consumed WHERE token = $token RETURNING *
There is no AND status = Active predicate. Both concurrent writers succeed.

packages/core/src/libraries/one-time-token.ts#verifyOneTimeToken() performs a read-then-write: checkOneTimeToken() reads and validates the token is Active, then updateOneTimeTokenStatus() updates to Consumed without checking current status.

Under PostgreSQL Read Committed:
- T1 reads status=Active (passes check)
- T2 reads status=Active (passes check, T1 has not committed yet)
- T1 UPDATE to Consumed, commits
- T2 UPDATE to Consumed (finds row by token, no status predicate - succeeds)

## Affected Routes

- Management API: POST /api/one-time-tokens/verify
- Experience API: POST /experience/verification/one-time-token/verify
- Forgot-password flow: identifyForgotPasswordWithOneTimeToken()

## Proof

PostgreSQL-backed concurrency test: 30/30 race iterations both transactions successfully verified the same Active token (100% reproduction).

## Remediation

Add AND status = Active to the UPDATE WHERE clause:
  UPDATE one_time_tokens SET status = Consumed WHERE token = $token AND status = Active RETURNING *
